subject: Recap & next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing (FinTech Co.)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@fintech-co.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing questions and next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time today, and great demo from your side. Quick recap + the sizing inputs we need to build a firm dedicated capacity proposal for FinTech Co.:

Summary of what we discussed
- You’re evaluating Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) vs Hosted API for production due to predictable throughput and data isolation needs. Private/VPC is on the roadmap for procurement but pilot will be on Redwood Dedicated.
- Pilot target: early June (target start ~2027-06-01).

Sizing questions / asks (please confirm):
1) Target sustained TPS (average requests per second) and peak TPS (15 min peak)
2) Typical concurrency (# of in-flight requests you expect at peak)
3) Average prompt length (tokens) and average completion length (tokens). If you have distribution (10/50/90 pct) that’s extra helpful.
4) Token mix: % generation / % embeddings / % reranking
5) Latency SLO (p95) and any hard SLA thresholds for tail latency
6) Preferred GPU types (if any) or cost vs latency trade-offs we should assume (H100 vs A100 vs L4)
7) Region/data residency requirements (we noted US-west preferred)
8) Compliance items: SOC2 / encryption / audit logs — anything beyond standard SOC2 that procurement needs?
9) Any burst/seasonality (e.g., marketing campaign days) and expected growth over 6/12 months

Attachments you can share: traffic_sample.csv or an API log sample will let us run a realistic sizing sim; procurement/RFP doc also helpful.

Next steps
- If you can reply to the questions above, Rafael and I will produce a ballpark Dedicated config (GPU count/type, estimated concurrent capacity, throughput, and monthly committed cost) within 2 business days.
- We’ll follow with a short call to walk the assumptions and trade-offs.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced: redwood_dedicated_ballpark.xlsx (we’ll populate once you confirm numbers)

From: John Lee <john.lee@fintech-co.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTech Co. Procurement <procurement@fintech-co.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing questions and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Answers below and I attached the RFP + a small traffic sample.

Answers to sizing questions
1) Sustained TPS: 15 requests/sec average. Peak TPS (15-min): ~60 requests/sec.
2) Concurrency at peak: expect ~30 concurrent in-flight requests during peak windows.
3) Token lengths: average prompt ~120 tokens, average completion ~240 tokens. 90th pct completion ~800 tokens (rare but happens for long explanations).
4) Token mix: ~70% generation (chat/assistant), ~25% embeddings (vector searches for context), ~5% reranking.
5) Latency SLO: p95 <= 600ms for generation requests. Hard SLA: if p95 exceeds 1s we escalate.
6) GPU preference: we don’t have a hard preference — open to H100 if cost is reasonable; A100 acceptable if you can meet latency. Cost matters but we prioritize consistent p95.
7) Region: us-west required for data residency.
8) Compliance: SOC2 is required; we also need customer-managed KMS in deployment (we can discuss details with security).
9) Burst: expected spikes around product releases and monthly statements; spikes can be ~2x baseline and last 1–3 hours. Growth: plan for ~30% usage growth over 6 months post-pilot.

Attachments: FinTechCo_RFP_Q2.pdf, traffic_sample.csv

Let me know if you need sample logs in a different format. We’re happy to hop on a sizing call later this week.

—John
John Lee | Head of Product, FinTech Co.
john.lee@fintech-co.com | +1 (415) 555-9876

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@fintech-co.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing questions and next steps

Thanks John — that’s perfect and very helpful. We reviewed the traffic sample and Rafael and I sketched a conservative ballpark based on your inputs. High-level guidance (ballpark, not final pricing or commitment):

Ballpark recommendation (to meet p95 <= 600ms for generation with your token mix & peaks)
- Model family assumption: transformer LLM (large decoder-only) ~ generation-optimized (we’ll confirm exact model in the proposal).
- Recommended GPU tier: H100 80GB for best p95 and headroom. A100 80GB could work with tighter batching but H100 preferred for consistent tail latency.
- Initial Dedicated pool: 4 x H100 (4x 80GB GPUs) with autoscale buffer for 2x burst. This config targets sustained 15 TPS with headroom to 60 TPS peaks while keeping p95 < 600ms based on our sim.
- Concurrency: target pool to support ~30 concurrent in-flight generation requests; autoscaling policy to add capacity on sustained queue/backlog.

Operational notes and trade-offs
- If procurement prefers lower committed cost, we can propose 2 x H100 + aggressive autoscaling to A100 spot pools for non-critical background workloads (embeddings/batch jobs).
- If you plan to use very long completions routinely (90th pct ~800 tokens), we should size for those tails separately — they consume KV cache and GPU memory; we may recommend an additional H100 for heavy long-turn dialogues.
- KMS: we can enable customer-managed KMS for data at rest; Rafael will loop in Security for an onboarding checklist.

Next steps
1) Rafael will produce a short written proposal (GPU qty/type, expected concurrency, throughput targets, monthly committed cost, and a few options: conservative (4x H100), cost-optimized (2x H100 + burst), and A100 option). You’ll have this within 48 hours.
2) Schedule a 30-min call to review assumptions and finalize pilot scope — Rafael and I are available Thurs/Fri afternoon PT. Please share preferred times.
3) Procurement: we’ll respond to RFP questions; I’ll add a procurement owner from our side on the next thread.

Thanks — Rafael will take the lead on the written proposal.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
